body:
`searchBook` returns an empty result before touching the book for any trimmed query shorter than
`MIN_QUERY_LENGTH = 2` (frontend/src/lib/reader/searchBook.ts). The comment justifies it as
"never what the reader meant", and for Latin scripts that holds.

It is false for CJK and other scripts where a single visible character is a complete word. For
those books a whole class of valid in-book queries silently returns nothing -- and it returns
"nothing typed yet", not "no matches", so the reader gets no signal at all.

Not a cosmetic i18n nit: search is simply unusable for some queries in those languages.

Fixing it properly needs a script-aware rule (or a submit action / lower cap for potentially
expensive one-character scans) rather than lowering the constant, since the constant also exists
to stop a full-book scan on a query that matches everything.

Found by adversarial review (Terra) during the search-UI work; left unfixed deliberately so a
correctness decision about non-Latin books is not buried inside a UI PR.
title: Search rejects one-character queries, which are real words in CJK
